# REST API: Tokens

These routes of the platform API come from its [OpenAPI document](../openapi.json); [The REST API as a contract](../rest-api.md) says what Lakana promises about them.

## `POST /api/v1/principals/{name}/tokens`

Issue a personal access token

From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token is never asked for a touch, and a non-administrator's token cannot create a token at all.

Issues a token that signs in as the principal. The answer holds the token's full value, which is shown this once and cannot be read again. For another principal it needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance. For oneself, unless one is an administrator, it works only from the web interface: no token can create a token, so a stolen token cannot mint replacements (403). Answers 404 when there is no such principal.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The principal the PAT authenticates as. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `TokenIssueIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Successful Response | `TokenIssueOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `TokenIssueOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key_id` | text | yes |  |
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `token` | text | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/principals/{name}/tokens`

List the tokens of a principal

Lists the principal's personal access tokens. The token values are never included. Anyone may list their own with a personal token or a web session; anyone else's needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance, and is refused alike whether or not the principal exists. Answers 404 when there is no such principal.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The principal whose PATs to list. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | list of `TokenOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `DELETE /api/v1/principals/{name}/tokens/{key_id}`

Revoke a personal access token

The token stops working at once. Anyone may revoke their own with a personal token or a web session, without a passkey touch; anyone else's needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance. Answers 404 when the principal or the token does not exist.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The principal the PAT belongs to. |
| `key_id` | path | yes | text | The PAT's key_id. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |
